Department Information

Improving lives and communities through transportation.

Caltrans Vision:
A thriving and connected California.

The Caltrans workforce is made up of diverse and unique individuals who contribute to our organizational success.

Department Website: www.dot.ca.gov

Director’s EEO Policy : https://dot.ca.gov/programs/equal-employment-opportunity

Director’s EEO Policy Statement: https://dot.ca.gov/programs/equal-employment-opportunity

Job Description And Duties

Caltrans Environmental Scientists perform a broad range of work concerning environmental issues related to protecting California's resources as related to transportation projects. Incumbents do field analyses; prepare environmental documents and technical studies, environmental permitting packages and regulatory permits; ensure compliance with various environmental laws and regulations; and conduct environmental protection, planning, and mitigation activities. Incumbents apply scientific methods and principles to analyze and evaluate available data on the effects of transportation projects on all aspects of the environment; prepare and review CEQA/NEPA and other technical documents to determine the effects; and implement mitigation strategies to lessen the impact of those projects.

Under the general direction of the Environmental Branch Chief, the incumbent is an interdisciplinary team member who must establish and maintain a professional working relationship with internal project delivery partners, various regulatory agencies, local partners and interested parties involved with Caltrans' projects. The incumbent must be solution oriented and will need to investigate innovative solutions to meet deliverables. This work requires strong oral and written skills with the specific ability to prepare technical reports as well as written and verbal correspondence. This position may require site visits, sometimes to remote areas, which may require driving a personal or state vehicle on public roadways or on uneven terrain.

PARF# 04-26-0139 / JC-526611

This is an LT position with the possibility of becoming permanent.

This is a reposting of JC-509699. If you have previously applied to this position, you do not have to re-apply. Your application will be considered.

Eligibility for hire may be determined by your score on the Environmental Scientist exam. For those who do not have current eligibility (e.g., transfer, permissive reinstatement, or voluntary demotions) and/or who will be new to state civil services employment, you must be on the state examination list to be eligible for these positions. To apply for the exam, please click here and search by typing in the classification title.

Please take this 1-minute Caltrans Recruitment survey to tell us how you found out about this job.

https://forms.office.com/g/RyK102ty4G

https://youtu.be/oC9wIp8QalI

Apply today to join our team! We especially encourage applicants to check out our Caltrans Career Compass tool! The Caltrans Career Compass is a tool to assist and help candidates understand and succeed in applying to Caltrans positions.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Special Requirements

Possession of a valid driver’s license is required when operating a state owned or leased vehicle.
Statement of Qualification (SOQ) is required.

Please include a statement of qualifications (SOQ) that is no more than two pages typed, single spaced, using 12-point Arial font. Note that resumes and/or cover letters will not take the place of the SOQ. On your SOQ, please expand upon the prompts below and provide sufficient details on your career experience as it relates to each question. Provide sufficient detail with each question to indicate why you believe your knowledge, skills, and experience would make you the best candidate to take on the roles and responsibilities of this position. Your response should provide specific, job-related experiences that demonstrate the following:

Describe any relevant coursework and experience as they relate to the positions duty statement.
Please explain how you would coordinate a multi-disciplinary team with conflicting priorities and still meet tight delivery deadlines.
Provide an example of a time when you managed multiple projects simultaneously and the steps you took to ensure they were delivered.

Possession of Minimum Qualifications will be verified prior to interview and/or appointment. If you are basing your eligibility on education, you must include your unofficial transcript(s)/diploma for verification. Unofficial, original, or official sealed transcripts will be accepted and may be required upon appointment. Applicants with foreign transcripts/degrees must provide a transcript/degree U.S. equivalency report evaluation that indicates the number of units and degree to which the foreign coursework is equivalent. Please visit either of the following two websites for a list of evaluation agencies: https://www.naces.org/members or https://aice-eval.org . Please redact birthdates and social security numbers.

Individuals who are currently in the classification, eligible for lateral transfer, eligible for reinstatement, have list or LEAP eligibility, are in the process of obtaining list eligibility, or have SROA and/or Surplus eligibility (please attach your letter, if available). SROA and Surplus candidates are given priority; therefore, individuals with other eligibility may be considered in the event no SROA or Surplus candidates apply. Individuals who are eligible for a Training and Development assignment may also be considered for this position(s).

jobs.title: Regional Inside Sales Account Manager - Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, LLC
jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

The Regional Inside Sales Coordinator (RISC) serves as the administrative liaison for the sales team and actively seeks sales opportunities in smaller segments of the Water Testing market. The RISC is responsible for working with the sales staff to respond to quotes, Requests for Proposal (RFPs), purchase orders, and other client contractual issues as they arise. The RISC also pursues sales from targeted clients through phone calls and direct mail efforts. In all interactions, the RISC will act in the best interest of Eurofins and demonstrate professionalism and high performance when working with both internal and external clients. Eurofins and the RISC are committed to growing the business through a client-first culture that delivers exemplary service.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Conduct cold calls and sales campaigns to generate new sales.
Generate transactional price quotes as directed.
Conduct proposal research & provide technical support (Excel spreadsheet experience).
Onboard new accounts according to policy and complete vendor forms.
Assist in response to client inquiries originating from sales calls/emails.
Participate in sales campaigns to maintain and grow selected accounts/territories.
Ensure customer awareness of LIMS capabilities and services to improve selling opportunities.
Manage all subcontractor (within network and outside) issues (pricing/contacts/communications), including Project Management (PM) and sales rep requests for information from subcontract laboratories, while maintaining corporate purchasing directives to minimize volume to competitors and to be price sensitive.
Assist with proposal development, maintain proposal files.
Provide information to Account Managers and Directors on feedback received from clients regarding service issues and our competition.
Assist in the preparation for and attend periodic sales meetings as assigned.
Respond to requests for insurance certificates.
Establish and maintain a productive working relationship between client and lab.
Bid Portal(s) Listing Review (Bid Prime)
Manage processing of all awarded contract requirements.
TALS/LIMS experience familiarity is preferred.
Provide sister lab [ICO] research to gather info (capabilities, ability to meet RL's, verify parameter lists, certifications, correct method & prep codes)
Review Bid Portal(s) Listing and Review RFP documents for distribution (Bid Prime)
Maintain Competitor database by dissemination of bid tabulations
Maintain 3rd party laboratory database - pricing and capabilities
Understand contract requirements in obtaining client certificates of insurance
Provide support for annual price increases for contracted clients

Qualifications

Education: AS/AA degree in Business related field with environmental experience (3-4 years client-relationship experience may substitute the degree).
Experience: 1-3 years experience in environmental industry sales and marketing or sales/laboratory support role.
LIMS experience is a plus
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.

Additional Information

This is a full-time Exempt position. Role is Monday to Friday 9 am to 5pm with flexibility for longer hours and weekends.

compensation: $$71k-$82K (DOE).

Remote candidates are welcome to apply; candidates located in Pomona, CA or the West Coast are preferred.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

jobs.company: NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure
jobs.title: Environmental Assessment Officer
jobs.location: Harris Park, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Build your future with the team driving NSW communities, spaces and economies

Shape NSW's future through major project assessment and community outcomes.

Permanent full-time opportunity,

Office location based in Parramatta with flexible working supported

Salary relative to experience, and ranges from $119,329 to $134,463 + super

Join our team and shape your world in a workplace that empowers you to do your best work and build a meaningful career. In this role, you will contribute to shaping lives and communities across NSW, while shaping your own career. You will enjoy flexible work options, varied and impactful projects, and a vibrant, diverse team culture built on collaboration, inclusion and support. We are creating a workplace where everyone belongs and where you can balance work, life and wellbeing.

The role

As an Environmental Assessment Officer
in the Industry Assessment team, you will assess major projects across a wide range of interesting and dynamic sectors that help shape communities, support economic growth and deliver critical infrastructure across NSW. You'll provide expert planning advice that balances community expectations, government priorities and statutory requirements while helping drive better planning outcomes.

Working across a range of projects, you'll analyse complex information, prepare clear recommendations and engage with stakeholders to help deliver better outcomes for the state. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a real impact while shaping thriving and connected communities.

For more information about this position, read the full Role Description: Environmental Assessment Officer

What you will bring to the role

Ability to assess the merits of State significant projects quickly and effectively in sectors such as manufacturing and chemical industries, renewable fuels, the circular economy including large scale waste and recycling, data centres, agricultural and aquaculture, warehouse and distribution facilities, including within the Western Sydney Aerotropolis and State activation precincts.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, concise and accessible advice, reports and recommendations for diverse audiences.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to research, evaluate complex issues and develop practical solutions to support sound environmental assessment outcomes.
Outstanding stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective relationships, manage competing expectations and work collaboratively with government agencies, industry representatives, developers and community stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to prioritise competing workloads, manage multiple projects and deliver high-quality outcomes within demanding timeframes in a fast-paced environment.

What is an essential requirement:

Degree in environmental science or management, engineering, planning or other relevant discipline
Willingness to travel and (minimum) Class C Driver’s License.

About Us

At the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI), you could shape your world while helping us shape the future of NSW. Together, we create vibrant communities, places and precincts, and manage land, assets and property.
(We are a high-performing organisation that proudly reflects the communities we serve. Our diversity strengthens our cultural capability and enables us to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people across NSW. As an inclusive and accessible workplace, we value your contribution, lived experience and cultural knowledge, and we want you to feel supported, connected and empowered to succeed. With flexible work arrangements, job share options, workplace adjustments and various employee affinity groups, we are here to help you thrive every day.
Join us

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, we encourage you to apply with your CV and cover letter. We’d love to hear from you and explore how you can shape your world with us. Applications close Sunday 16 Aug 2026 at 11:55pm
. Should you require further information about the role please contact Catriona Shirley (catriona.shirley@dpie.nsw.gov.au)

A talent pool may be created for ongoing and temporary opportunities of the same role or role type that may become available over the next 18 months.

Check out our Aboriginal applicants guide to assist with applying for the role or contact our Aboriginal Career pathways team for a yarn.
We encourage and support applications from people with disability. Please reach out to us to discuss any accommodations or adjustments that may be needed during the recruitment process, ensuring that you have every opportunity to showcase your talent, skills, and potential. Contact the Talent Team via talent.acquisition@dpie.nsw.gov.au or (02) 63637676​ - HR Support, option 2, DPHI People Advisory, option 1 and reference 'Request an Adjustment - Job Title and Reference Number'.
Please note to be eligible to apply for this position you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident or hold a valid Australian working Visa for the duration of the appointment. This role is subject to standard pre-employment checks, including a criminal record check.
